_comment: THIRD-PARTY INFRASTRUCTURE every site talks to — analytics, CDNs, managed mail, managed DNS. A shared entry here is same-PLATFORM, never same-OPERATOR. These lists are what stop a bundle-scraped analytics endpoint or a Cloudflare nameserver from being reported as the operator's backend. Add a provider the moment you see it show up as a bogus 'operator asset'.

backend_noise_suffixes._comment: Hostname suffixes that are NEVER the operator's backend, even when a JS bundle calls them. Matched exact-or-parent (foo.sentry.io is caught by sentry.io). Consumed by wp_assets._skip_backend when harvesting api_endpoint/websocket pivots out of JS bundles. Deliberately broader than the HTML-side CDN list: bundles reference far more third-party endpoints than the document does.

managed_mx_suffixes._comment: MX hostname suffixes belonging to a managed mail provider. Two domains sharing aspmx.l.google.com share Google, not an owner. Consumed by wp_ippivot when deciding whether an MX record is a pivot or context.

managed_ns_substrings._comment: Nameserver-host substrings that mark DNS-provider plumbing rather than operator infrastructure. Consumed by evidence_report._is_infra_noise_host to keep provider NS out of the report's Discovered Infrastructure table. NOTE: this is a SUBSTRING match by design (it also has to catch bare labels like 'awsdns'); the label-boundary version used for CLUSTERING lives in tools/kb/references/noise_filters.json -> managed_dns_suffixes.

boilerplate_email_hosts._comment: Email-host suffixes that are a PLATFORM's system addresses, never the site owner's: a Wix contact relay, a Sentry DSN host, a builder's support mailbox. An address at one of these is infrastructure, so it must not seed a contact or same-operator pivot.
